mechanism_narrative: High real GDP levels (GDPC1) correlate with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to sustained corporate earnings growth from strong economic activity, and this relationship holds consistently without requiring specific triggering conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when GDPC1 > 11000, or Rank IC for GDPC1 as predictor falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 5.0% triggers positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through reduced corporate financing costs and increased investment, as observed in historical monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 5.0, or Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as predictor is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly low unemployment (UNRATE) and strong employment growth (PAYEMS) signal positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through robust consumer spending, and this interaction effect is not decomposable into individual series impacts.
failure_condition: The interaction term between PAYEMS and UNRATE shows negative coefficient in regression models predicting 20-day returns, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO > 110) during late-cycle expansions drives positive 20-day S&P 500 returns via elevated manufacturing output supporting corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when INDPRO > 110 during late-cycle expansions, or Rank IC for INDPRO as predictor in late-cycle regimes is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above 1500.0 thousand units trigger positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through elevated consumer spending and economic activity, with the effect observable within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when HOUST > 1500.0, or Rank IC for HOUST as predictor falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 5.0 and FEDFUNDS rise > 0.5% in 3 months) cause negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to increased borrowing costs reducing corporate investment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0 and FEDFUNDS rise > 0.5% (3mo), or Rank IC for condition is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly high housing starts (HOUST > 1500) and strong retail sales (RSAFS > 370000) drive positive 60-day S&P 500 returns through amplified consumer demand, with the interaction effect not explained by either series alone.
failure_condition: The interaction term between HOUST and RSAFS shows negative coefficient in regression models predicting 60-day returns, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers positive 20-day S&P 500 returns via tight labor market conditions supporting wage growth and consumer spending, with the effect most pronounced in stable economic regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.5, or Rank IC for UNRATE as predictor falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
